title: Released Emails Show ICE Coordinated Deportation Flights to Iran, Let Tehran Influence Passenger Lists
detail: Hundreds of emails obtained via a Freedom of Information Act request by the National Iranian American Council and published August 20, 2026 (reported first by the Associated Press) reveal that ICE officials coordinated directly with the Iranian government — often through Qatari intermediaries — to arrange three deportation flights returning more than 100 Iranian nationals to Iran in September and December 2025 and January 2026. The emails show Iranian officials repeatedly influenced who was placed on the manifests: one ICE official wrote 'Per request from the Iran Embassy I added a few cases,' and another said Iran had 'requested that I amend the previous manifest and expedite the removal process,' with the Iranian Embassy still requesting additions as recently as three days before a September flight's departure. On several occasions ICE arranged for Iranian officials to meet directly with detainees in U.S. custody; eleven detained Iranians said they were forced into such meetings. The coordination continued through the June 2025 U.S.-Israel-Iran conflict. Iranian officials had said as many as 400 Iranians could be returned under the arrangement, though the completed flights were smaller. DHS declined to comment on the emails but has previously and separately denied sharing asylum records with Iran, calling such claims 'FALSE.'

title: First ICE Deportation Flight to Haiti Since TPS Termination Lands in Cap-Haïtien
detail: An ICE charter aircraft carrying 161 Haitian nationals departed Alexandria, Louisiana and landed in Cap-Haïtien, Haiti's second-largest city, shortly before noon on Thursday, August 20, 2026 — the first deportation flight to Haiti since the Trump administration terminated Temporary Protected Status last month for more than 300,000 Haitians in the U.S., and the eighth deportation flight to Haiti in 2026 overall. The flight landed in Cap-Haïtien rather than the capital Port-au-Prince because the U.S. government maintains a ban on commercial flights to Port-au-Prince through early September 2026 over ongoing gang violence. Haiti's National Office of Migration said the group included people placed in removal proceedings after entering illegally, deportees who had completed criminal sentences, and individuals born outside Haiti — including in Chile and the Dominican Republic — but sent there because a parent was Haitian. Returnees received roughly $76.40 from the Haitian government, short of the $250 fare to reach Port-au-Prince. U.S. officials said flights will increase to twice weekly, returning about 250 Haitians per week. U.N. spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said the U.N. team in Haiti is 'stretched' but doing what it can to support the government's reintegration effort.

title: ICE Detains 'Beloved' Haitian Pastor Gilbert Joubert Adrien in Springfield, Ohio
detail: ICE agents detained Gilbert Joubert Adrien, 41, a pastor described by community members as a beloved leader of Springfield, Ohio's Haitian community, at a Sunoco gas station on South Limestone Street on Thursday, August 20, 2026. Another Haitian man, Victor Yonel, was also taken into custody in the same stop; a woman who was in the car with them was released. Adrien is being held at the Butler County Jail in Hamilton, Ohio, according to the DHS detainee locator. The Haitian Support Center said Adrien has a pending asylum case that advocates believed should have shielded him from detention. G92, a Springfield faith-advocacy group, called the detention 'a profound wound' to the community; member Marjory Wentworth said 'the community is really deeply saddened. It makes everyone feel even more vulnerable,' while Haitian Support Center executive director Vilés Dorsainvil warned that if Adrien is deported, 'the congregation will be here terrified and without their leader.' More than two dozen Haitians with Springfield connections have been detained and held at Butler County Jail in recent weeks as ICE intensifies enforcement following the July 27, 2026 termination of TPS for the city's roughly 15,000-strong Haitian community.
